guides.explanation_en: 发 contributes sending or bringing something forth, while 出 adds the idea that it goes outward or emerges. Together, 发出 means to send something out, or to produce something such as a signal or sound.

parts.contribution_en: Contributes sending or bringing something forth.
Adds outward direction or emergence.

claims.text_en: The dictionaries support a broad modern range for 發出: transmitting or sending something out, expressing something, and producing a sound. The supplied sentence establishes that its instance refers to sending out a signal. The opened dictionary examples do not specifically attest that signal collocation, so the context supports that subcase rather than the dictionary examples themselves.

A cautious component-level paraphrase is that 發 can contribute sending, bringing forth, or expressing, while 出 can contribute outward direction or an achieved effect. This is compatible with the dictionary definitions of 發出, but those sources do not provide a word-specific grammatical or historical analysis; the paraphrase should not be treated as a proven derivation.

Research on verb-resultative constructions discusses 出来 as a result complement and general references distinguish directional and extended result uses of complements. These descriptions concern broader constructions and do not show that modern 發出 is a V+result-complement form or derives from one.

guides.explanation_en: 取得 means to obtain or attain something, including an outcome such as a victory. 取 evokes taking or obtaining, while 得 evokes getting or coming to have; their overlapping contributions present the thing as gained.
guides.caveat_en: The parts overlap in meaning rather than marking two sharply separate steps.

parts.contribution_en: Evokes taking or obtaining.

guides.explanation_en: 国家 is the conventional word for a country or nation: a political community understood as a whole. One historical account explains its parts through the fiefs of lords and senior officials: 国 referred to a lord’s domain, while 家 could refer to a senior official’s estate or governed domain. Another scholarly account describes 家’s family living-space sense taking on a political sense and 国 and 家 blending into the compound; these accounts do not establish one certain path for every early use.
guides.caveat_en: The fief pairing is a reported historical explanation, not proof that every early use of 国家 arose directly from those two domains. Historical accounts differ in their emphasis and dating.

parts.contribution_en: In the historical fief account, the domain of a lord; in the present-day word, part of the term for a country or polity.
Historically, it could mean a senior official’s estate or governed domain, extending beyond the sense of a household; one account connects this political sense with family living space.

sources.title: 中华思想文化术语“国家”的中文解释及英文翻译
sources.summary_en: Describes ancient 国家 as a combined term for the fiefs of lords and senior officials, says it later referred to a country’s whole territory, and describes its modern political-entity sense. It also connects family, clan, and state with kinship and lineage organization.

sources.title: The Formation and Changes of GuoJia(國家, state & country) Idea in Ancient Chinese Political Thought
sources.summary_en: The accessible abstract of a 2015 Korean Political Science Review article characterizes 家 first as family living space associated with ancestral rites, then as political space governed by a senior official under Zhou enfeoffment and clan policies. It argues that 国 and 家 blended into 国家 during the Warring States period.

claims.text_en: In ancient political usage, 家 could refer to the stipend estate or governed domain of a senior official, rather than simply a household. The Han Dian Guoyu entry distinguishes that 家 from a lord’s 国; the specialist terminology entry similarly describes 家 as a dafu’s fief.

One specialist terminology account presents 国家 as a combined term for those two kinds of fief and describes a later extension to a country’s whole territory and then to a modern political entity. This supports a historical political contribution for 家, but is that source’s account of development rather than proof that every early use followed this path.

A scholarly article abstract gives a related but distinct account: 家’s family living-space sense became political space under Zhou institutions, and 国 and 家 blended into 国家 during the Warring States period. The current sense “country; nation” is also supported by Han Dian’s definition of 国家 as a political group and its translations.

claims.text_en: In the supplied sentence, 发现 means that the three people noticed or realized that there were many enemies. The context supports awareness of a situation; it does not say that they discovered a new principle or located an object.

The attestations document a range of senses, but do not by themselves prove that the modern awareness use developed from any particular older sense.

Modern dictionaries also list object-location and research-based finding uses of 发现. Those are valid uses of the spelling, but they are not needed to interpret the supplied sentence, where the object of awareness is the situation that many enemies are present.

The opened historical-method article recommends establishing first attestations, sound evidence, and semantic links when tracing vocabulary history. It does not analyze 发现, so it supports caution in method rather than any specific account of this word's origin.

许多 means “many” or “a large number of.” It is used as a whole quantity word; 多 suggests numerousness, but 许 does not add a reliably separate degree meaning.
guides.caveat_en: Treat 许多 as a whole rather than reading 许 as an independent intensifier meaning “very.”

sources.title: “许+形”式短语与词汇研究
sources.summary_en: This study says modern 许多 means 很多 or 非常多 and is a lexical whole whose 许 cannot simply be analyzed as a degree adverb modifying 多. It proposes that older 许+adjective forms developed from 如许+adjective constructions meaning roughly 'such/this much + adjective', and that emphatic uses grew in particular sentence patterns. It cites older examples, including 如许多 and 许多, but its proposed historical development does not independently prove the derivation of the modern quantity word.

sources.title: 韵律构词与问数词“许多”的形成
sources.summary_en: Feng He distinguishes the Ming–Qing interrogative 许多 ('how many/how much') from quantity-denoting 许多. The abstract proposes that the interrogative form arose from 几许+多 through deletion of 几. In a note, the author says ordinary quantity 许多 became common from the Qing period, cites examples, and refers to a separate 2014 study for the proposed antecedents 尔许多 or 如许多. This page supports the distinction and reports the scholarly proposal, but does not provide the full text of that separate study.

sources.title: 汉典：许多
sources.summary_en: Lists quantity-denoting 许多, interrogative 许多, and an emphatic large-quantity or degree use separately, with historical examples. This is useful for identifying distinct senses; the entry does not establish how the target sense developed.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 许多 as a whole means 'many' or 'a large number of'; the Ministry of Education dictionary equates it with 很多 and illustrates it with people. The definition and example do not identify a narrower kind of quantity.

For present-day quantity 许多, the specialist study treats the expression as a lexical whole and cautions against assigning 许 the independent synchronic function of a degree adverb such as 很 or 非常. On this evidence, 许 need not be given a separate modern contribution distinct from 多.

A specialist historical account proposes that 许+adjective forms developed from constructions such as 如许+多, with 如许 conveying a demonstrative quantity or degree ('such/this much'). The study cites older examples and argues for continuity, but that analysis is a proposed historical path; the material opened here does not independently establish every step as the derivation of the modern quantity word 许多.

The spelling 许多 also occurs as an interrogative meaning 'how many/how much'. Feng He distinguishes that use from the supplied declarative quantity sense and proposes 几许+多 as the interrogative use's source. That proposed account concerns the interrogative sense, not the origin of target-sense 许多.

guides.explanation_en: 听 means to hear or listen by ear, and 了 marks that event as actualized. In a sequence, the hearing can be understood as preceding a later event or reaction, giving 听了 the sense “after hearing/listening.” 了 does not itself mean “after” or specify past time.
guides.caveat_en: The “after” relation depends on the surrounding sequence or context; it is not an invariant meaning of every verb followed by 了.

A postverbal perfective marker that presents the hearing event as actualized, without specifying past time by itself.

sources.title: Tense and aspect in Mandarin Chinese — CityUHK Scholars
sources.summary_en: Meichun Liu’s chapter abstract distinguishes perfective le, which marks an event as actualized, from sentence-final le. It says Mandarin lacks grammaticalized tense and that event time can be inferred from time adverbs, aspect markers, or context.

sources.title: The Aspectual System of Mandarin Chinese — Suying Yang dissertation
sources.summary_en: Yang discusses le as a perfective marker and gives a sequence example that can be understood in either past or future time: the le-marked eating event precedes the subsequent visit. This supports the possibility of temporal sequencing with le in discourse, not a universal ‘after’ meaning for every V-le phrase.

claims.text_en: In the supplied auditory sense, 听 contributes hearing or listening by ear. The dictionary also records other senses of 听, but they do not match the supplied example’s auditory reading.

Postverbal 了 contributes perfective aspect: Liu describes it as marking an event as actualized. It does not by itself establish past time; the event’s temporal location may depend on context or other material.

In the supplied example, the natural reading is that Liu Bei became happy after hearing or listening. This fits a discourse sequence in which the 了-marked event precedes a following event or reaction. The ‘after’ relation is contextual and should not be treated as a standalone meaning of 了 in every occurrence.

Here 了 follows 听 and is not at the end of the sentence; the dictionary distinguishes this postverbal use from sentence-final or pause-position 了. A reusable gloss for this supplied sense is ‘after hearing/listening,’ while recognizing that this paraphrase includes the contextual relation to what follows.

sources.title: “从”的介词化源义及其发展
sources.summary_en: The article abstract proposes ‘pass through’ and ‘accompany/follow’ as source senses in different syntactic contexts, which it associates with grammaticalization into spatial and dative prepositions. The accessible material is the abstract, not the full article.

claims.text_en: In 张飞举矛刺中邓茂，他从马上掉下, 从 introduces 马 as the spatial source or place from which the fall occurs: he falls from the horse. The sentence does not specify a more precise manner of falling.

Here 从 contributes a spatial source relation to the movement expressed by 掉下. The grammar reference also lists other starting-point uses of 从, including time and range; those are not the use shown in this example.

Historical accounts propose links between prepositional 从 and older verbal senses such as ‘follow/accompany’ and ‘pass through.’ One account proposes a path from ‘follow’ through ‘pass via’ to prepositional route and source uses; another distinguishes ‘pass through’ and ‘accompany/follow’ source senses in different grammaticalization contexts. These proposals do not by themselves establish the exact historical path of the modern construction meaning ‘fall from a horse.’

claims.text_en: In this military use, 三 contributes the count three and 路 contributes routes or lines of movement. The Ministry of Education dictionary explicitly gives 兵分三路 as an example under 路線, and the 封神演義 passage uses 三路分兵 for troops assigned to separate routes toward passes.

In the supplied 三路夾攻 context, 三路 refers to three coordinated attacking contingents or approaches: the narrative identifies forces on the left and right and Liu Bei's force turning back to attack. The word 路 by itself denotes routes or lines, so translating the phrase contextually as “three attacking forces” is supported by the passage, rather than by 三路 as a fixed standalone meaning. The exact compass directions are not specified.

夾攻 contributes the attack-from-the-sides or pincer-attack notion. The cited dictionary describes this as attack from the left and right; in the supplied passage that meaning combines with the three contingents to describe their coordinated assault. It does not establish a precise formation beyond what the narrative states.

sources.title: 关于“就”字的释义
sources.summary_en: This page reproduces dictionary-style entries that distinguish adverbial 就 for an event occurring early or ending early from 就 for an event occurring within a short time and for sequential events. Its example 他十五岁就参加革命了 supports the early-time classification. The page is hosted by a university office, rather than being the dictionary itself.

sources.title: 从“就”看词义的形成、分项和识别
sources.summary_en: Zuo Simin’s article describes the early-occurrence reading and distinguishes it from the imminent/short-time and sequential readings. It argues that early occurrence can be a pragmatic implication of a short-time meaning in a suitable temporal and aspectual context; this is the author’s analysis, not an uncontested derivation. It also records older verbal senses such as moving toward, returning, or taking up a post, but does not document their development into the modern early-time use.

sources.title: 你了解“就”的用法吗？ / Consejos prácticos para el uso correcto del adverbio jiù
sources.summary_en: An Instituto Confucio language article distinguishes early occurrence, commonly preceded by a time expression, from occurrence within a short time and from sequential events. Its examples include 从小 and other time expressions before 就. It supports the target construction pattern, though its example 从小我们就是好朋友 also contains 是 and is not identical to the supplied sentence.

claims.text_en: In 刘备家里很穷，从小就有大志, 从小 sets the temporal frame as childhood onward. 就 marks the state 有大志 as true from that early point; the sentence does not specify a more exact age or date. This is the early-occurrence use, not the imminent-use meaning. The dictionary-style entry classifies this early reading separately and illustrates it with 他十五岁就参加革命了; the specialist article describes temporal material before 就 as a diagnostic context for the early reading.

The supplied sense is distinct from 就 meaning that something will happen within a short time, as in 我就来, and from 就 linking successive events. The ECNU article proposes that the early reading may be inferred pragmatically from a more general short-time meaning in an appropriate context. That proposal helps explain the reading but does not establish a historical derivation for 从小就.

The cited article also reports older verbal uses of 就, including movement toward and arrival or return. Those attestations do not by themselves show that the modern early-time adverb developed from those verbal uses; the article does not establish that derivation.

parts.contribution_en: The whole word: lacking order, or unsettled and chaotic.

sources.title: 亂 : ㄌㄨㄢˋ — Ministry of Education Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
sources.summary_en: Taiwan’s Ministry of Education dictionary defines 亂 as ‘without order or system’ and separately as ‘unsettled, unstable,’ with examples and older citations. It also records a positive ‘orderly; able to govern’ sense, alongside senses such as rebellion, confusion, and arbitrary action.

sources.title: 漢語多功能字庫：亂
sources.summary_en: The CUHK database interprets the bronze form 𤔔 as an early form of 亂, depicting hands working with thread or silk floss and giving ‘manage silk’ as the original sense. It proposes that unarranged thread accounts for the disordered sense, while handling the thread accounts for ‘manage/order.’ It also reports bronze uses interpreted as ‘manage’ and notes other readings or interpretations of graphic details.

sources.title: 說文解字「亂」 — Shuowen.org
sources.summary_en: The page gives the received Shuowen gloss 治也 (‘govern; put in order’) and Duan Yucai’s emendation 不治也 (‘not governed/in order’). Duan treats the positive sense as a transferred use: because what is disordered needs governing, 亂 can also mean ‘govern.’ This records Duan’s analysis rather than establishing the full historical derivation of the modern adjective.

sources.title: 楊琪：說“治” — Fudan University Center for the Study of Unearthed Texts and Paleography
sources.summary_en: Yang Qi argues that the Shuowen graph glossed 亂 as 治 (‘govern’) is an ancient form of 治, disputing Duan Yucai’s insertion of 不. The article uses transmitted and excavated graph forms to support its proposal. This is a competing specialist interpretation of the graph and positive ‘govern’ usage, not evidence that the modern adjective derives from that positive sense.

sources.title: 李春桃：說何簋銘文中的“亂”字 — Fudan University Center for the Study of Unearthed Texts and Paleography
sources.summary_en: Li Chuntao argues that a disputed inscription graph in the He gui is 亂 and means ‘govern,’ citing the Shuowen, transmitted texts, and bronze graphs. The article demonstrates continued scholarly discussion of identifying and interpreting early graphs and positive uses; it does not establish a derivation for the modern ‘disordered’ adjective.

sources.title: 亂 luàn — 汉典
sources.summary_en: Han Dian records modern and historical senses of 亂, including ‘without order/system’ and ‘unsettled/unstable,’ plus citations for both disorderly and positive governing uses. Its Shuowen and Duan Yucai sections reproduce the received gloss and Duan’s emendation. It supports the sense distinction but is not independent evidence for a semantic derivation.

claims.text_en: The supplied sense ‘disordered; chaotic’ is supported for 亂: the Ministry of Education dictionary defines it as ‘without order or system’ and separately includes ‘unsettled, unstable.’ For the example about 天下 becoming 乱, ‘chaotic’ fits the documented general disorder/social instability range; it does not require a narrower kind of disorder.

The historical sources record opposing uses or analyses: Shuowen’s received text glosses 亂 as 治 (‘govern; put in order’), while Duan Yucai emends it to 不治 (‘not in order’) and explains ‘govern’ as a transferred sense. The dictionary also records positive governing usage separately from the negative disorder sense. These contrasts should not be collapsed into a single gloss.

CUHK proposes a composition-based account in which the bronze graph depicts hands working with thread or silk floss; unarranged thread is disordered, while working it produces the ‘govern/order’ sense. This is the database’s proposed account, not independently established proof that the modern adjective developed through this precise semantic path.

A Fudan paleography article advances a competing analysis of the Shuowen graph, arguing that it is an ancient form of 治 rather than a graph meaning 不治. Another Fudan article argues for a bronze use of 亂 meaning ‘govern.’ These discussions reinforce that the early graph and positive historical use require careful distinction from the well-attested modern negative adjective; neither article demonstrates the modern adjective’s derivation.

guides.explanation_en: 同心 combines 同, “shared” or “together,” with 心, “thought” or “intention.” It describes people whose minds or intentions are aligned, and so who share a purpose.

parts.contribution_en: Shared or together; marks the mental orientation as joint.
Thought or intention; gives the shared alignment its mental focus.

sources.summary_en: Lists 心 meanings including thought, intention, feeling, deliberation, and temperament. It also notes the traditional association of 心 with thinking.

claims.text_en: In the target sense, 同 contributes sharedness or jointness, while 心 contributes mental orientation, thought, or intention. Together they describe people aligned in mind or purpose, consistent with the dictionary’s definition 齊心、團結一致.

The dictionary distinguishes this united or aligned sense from other uses of 同心, including 志同道合, a confidant, a shared wish or ideal, and sharing a center. Those uses do not replace the supplied united-purpose sense.
The learner dictionary equates 同心 with 齊心 and illustrates it in 同心協力 and 同心同德. The example sentence supplies the purpose of rescuing the people; that goal is not part of the reusable meaning of 同心.

The revised dictionary cites 《易經·繫辭上》 and 《國語·晉語四》 for the united-mind sense. These citations attest older textual uses as presented by the dictionary, but do not establish a particular historical derivation of the modern word.

guides.explanation_en: 相信 means to believe or trust a person, or to regard a statement or idea as true. 信 contributes the central idea of believing or trusting. With a person as its target, the word does not specify exactly what is believed about them.
guides.caveat_en: The contribution of 相 to the modern word is not established, so 信 helps explain the meaning but does not account for the whole form.

parts.contribution_en: Its contribution to the modern meaning of the word is not established.
Contributes the central idea of believing or trusting.

sources.title: 汉典：相信的意思
sources.summary_en: Gives a general definition and separate senses for trusting someone and taking something to be true. It cites a 《史记》 example about ministers not trusting one another and reports an encyclopedia gloss of the 《谷梁传》 occurrence as mutual trust.

sources.title: 易混淆词语“相信—信任”的语义特征与形式搭配辨析
sources.summary_en: The specialist comparison says both 相信 and 信任 can take person-denoting objects, but 相信 also takes propositional complements and generally differs in meaning and collocations from 信任. It says 相信 is generally not used reciprocally in the way 相互信任 is. It does not explain the historical formation of 相信.

sources.title: 基于语料特点判断的上古出土文献某字存否研究——以“信”字为例
sources.summary_en: This scholarly article surveys early uses of 信 in transmitted texts, including uses glossed as believing or trusting. Its subject is whether the character 信 existed in early excavated documents; it does not analyze the compound 相信 or prove a derivation for it.

sources.title: 相信_词语「相信」解释什么意思_相信 的解释及出处 - 汉语词典
sources.summary_en: A secondary dictionary page reports historical senses including mutual trust, trust in another person, and the modern sense of regarding something as true. It cites the 《谷梁传》 and 《史记》, but the page itself does not establish a historical pathway between those senses.

claims.text_en: For 相信张角, the available context supports believing or trusting Zhang Jiao as a person. The wording does not specify what people believed about him or establish whether the emphasis is his reliability, his claims, or belief in him more broadly.

The modern word’s belief/trust meaning is semantically consistent with 信 as the content-bearing part; this is a component-level inference, not an explicit analysis in the opened sources. Early uses of 信 glossed as believing or trusting are separately reported, but they do not establish how the compound 相信 formed.

Historical dictionary reports describe an early reciprocal sense of 相信 as mutual trust, including a 《谷梁传》 citation, and a later interpersonal trust use in 《史记》. These attestations show older uses of the compound but do not prove that the modern nonreciprocal use developed from them.

The modern interpersonal target is distinct from the propositional sense ‘regard something as true.’ The specialist comparison confirms that 相信 can take either person-denoting objects or propositions, and notes that 相信 generally is not reciprocal like 相互信任.

parts.contribution_en: Contributes the sense of ordinary or usual.

sources.summary_en: Separately gives 平日，平常时候 and 太平时日, with Tang and Song literary citations for each. This records dictionary-classified older uses, but does not prove that one developed from the other.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 平时 means ordinary or usual times. Dictionaries distinguish this from a separate use meaning a peaceful period or peacetime; the supplied sentence supports the ordinary-times reading.

A cautious present-day compositional reading is that 平 contributes an ordinary/usual quality and 时 contributes time or occasion. The character entries make this reading plausible, but do not demonstrate that the modern word historically arose by combining those senses.
In the supplied example, 平时 frames selling shoes and straw mats as what he does in ordinary times. The sentence does not specify a frequency or schedule.

The dictionaries cite Tang-period uses under both the ordinary-times sense and the peaceful-period sense. These are evidence that both uses were recorded in older texts, not proof of the historical relationship or direction of development between them.

sources.summary_en: The accessible abstract reports a corpus-based comparison of 只好, 只得, and 只有. It characterizes 只好 as favoring a suitable choice after subjective weighing, with an implied acceptability nuance. The page does not provide the full article.

sources.title: 只好的解釋 | 漢典
sources.summary_en: The entry gives the modern compelled-choice sense and reproduces examples for other senses, including an older ‘then/thereupon’ use and ‘only permissible/possible.’ These distinct senses do not establish the history of the target sense.

claims.text_en: In the target sense, 只好 means that the actor can only take, or has to take, a course of action; the Ministry of Education dictionary describes it as making do when there is no alternative. This supports the supplied ‘have no choice but to’ sense without specifying the nature of the constraint.

A 2026 comparative-study abstract reports that 只好 tends to present a suitable choice after subjective weighing and to imply acceptability. This is a scholarly characterization of the word's usage, not a demonstrated account of 好's historical or morphemic contribution.

只好 also has dictionary-recorded uses distinct from the target compelled-choice sense, including ‘just/right at’ a time. The dictionary evidence for those uses does not show that they developed into the target sense.

guides.explanation_en: 和 links equal-status words or phrases, often nouns or pronouns, meaning “and.” It can also introduce a person who joins someone in an activity or is the other party in an interaction, meaning “with.”
guides.caveat_en: In a phrase such as 我和你一起做事, 和 may link “I” and “you,” or mark “you” as a companion; the wording can allow both readings.

sources.title: 並列を表す接続詞「和」「跟」「同」「与」「及」「以及」 | 中国語文法辞典
sources.summary_en: This grammar reference identifies conjunction 和 as connecting coordinate elements, including noun phrases and pronouns, and gives 我和她 as an example. It says 和 can also connect verb and adjective phrases, and that in a list of three or more items it commonly occurs between the final two.

sources.title: 相手を表す介詞「跟」「和」「同」「与」「向」「朝」「对」「给」「问」 | 中国語文法辞典
sources.summary_en: This reference describes prepositional 和 as introducing either a participant acting together with someone or a counterpart toward whom an action is directed. Its examples distinguish those patterns, including 我和家人一起去旅游 and 我有话要和你说. The latter is relevant to 和有志的人交朋友, where the person is the partner in the interaction.

sources.title: “和”“与”“同”的用法（杜老师语文信箱） | 人民日报海外版
sources.summary_en: The article says 和 can be a conjunction or preposition, though it is more often a conjunction. It illustrates conjunction 和 linking nouns, verbs, and adjectives, with coordinated elements at equal status. It is a usage discussion, not a historical account.

sources.title: 上古漢語伴隨動詞的語法化探究 | 期刊論文
sources.summary_en: The opened journal page gives the abstract of Wang Jinhui’s article. It describes a proposed grammaticalization path from comitative verb to comitative preposition to coordinate conjunction, and explicitly says the comitative prepositions 共、和、同、跟 that emerged after the Medieval period followed that path. The page provides the abstract but not the article’s examples or detailed argument.

claims.text_en: In the supplied coordination sense, 和 connects coordinate items such as nouns or pronouns. In a phrase such as 我和你, it marks the coordination relation between 我 and 你; it does not specify an action they perform. The sources also document 和 between the final two items in lists of three or more.

In the supplied “with” sense, 和 introduces a person who participates with the subject or serves as the counterpart in an interaction. In 和有志的人交朋友, the phrase identifies the person with whom the subject is willing to make friends; 和 is not linking two noun phrases as coordinated items.

The conjunction and preposition uses are grammatically distinguishable: conjunction 和 links elements on both sides, while prepositional 和 introduces a participant or counterpart associated with the following action. 我和你一起做大事 permits a coordination reading (“you and I”) and a comitative reading (“I, together with you”); 一起 is compatible with the latter but does not by itself rule out the former.

A scholarly article’s abstract proposes the development path comitative verb → comitative preposition → coordinate conjunction and explicitly includes 和 among the comitative prepositions said to have followed that path after the Medieval period. This is the author’s historical analysis; the opened abstract alone does not expose its dated examples or establish the detailed chronology independently.

guides.explanation_en: 敌 means “enemy” or “opponent,” and 人 means “person.” Together, they mean a person who bears enmity toward and opposes one’s side; the opposition need not be military.

parts.contribution_en: enemy or opponent
person

claims.text_en: In the supplied sense, 敵人 means a person who has enmity toward and opposes one’s side. The dictionary example shows that opposing positions can make former friends 敵人; the word is not restricted to a military enemy.

The word has a transparent component reading: 敵 contributes ‘enemy/opponent’ and 人 contributes ‘person.’ This is a supported word-part analysis; the dictionaries define 敵人 as a whole and do not present this segmentation as a historical derivation.

An older cited use of 敵人 occurs in Wenxin Diaolong in a discussion of argumentation, where an adversary might exploit a weakness. Han Dian also cites the compound from Guanzi. These attestations support an adversarial use of the compound, but do not show the precise historical path by which it formed or developed.

Shuowen glosses 敵 with 仇, and Duan Yucai’s note discusses related adversarial and contending senses. This contextualizes 敵 but does not prove that those older senses directly produced the modern compound’s meaning.

guides.explanation_en: 能 comes before a predicate to say that the subject can do it, either through their ability or because circumstances make it possible. In some contexts it can express permission too; the word alone does not specify the basis.

parts.contribution_en: A modal that marks the following action as within the subject’s ability or possible under relevant conditions; context determines the basis.

It separately records the noun sense “ability/talent.” Its quoted Shuowen account describes 能 as a bear-like animal and connects “worthy/capable” and “strong” senses with that description; the entry does not establish that this character history is the derivation of the modern modal.

sources.title: 助動詞 - 中国語文法辞典
sources.summary_en: This Chinese grammar reference distinguishes 能 for ability based on the subject’s own capacity, ability under objective conditions, and permission. Its examples illustrate the categories, but do not determine which contextual source of ability applies to the supplied sentence.

claims.text_en: In the target modal use, 能 precedes a predicate and marks that the action is within the subject’s ability or possible under relevant conditions. 董卓能不能活下来 asks whether Dong Zhuo can survive; the sentence does not specify which abilities or circumstances determine the outcome.

The dictionary records 能 as an older noun meaning ability or talent and cites early modal examples, including Xunzi’s 非能水也. These attestations show that both uses are old, but do not by themselves prove a historical derivation from the noun sense to the modal. Shuowen’s account of the character’s animal sense likewise does not establish that derivation.

能 can express ability based on personal capacity, objective conditions, or permission in different contexts. The supplied sentence supports a general question about whether survival is possible, but does not identify a permission reading or a more specific source of possibility.

guides.explanation_en: 命 is a verb meaning to direct or order someone to perform an action. It presents that action as something the person or group is told to carry out.

claims.text_en: In the target verb use, 命 means to direct, assign, or order someone to perform an action. 汉典 distinguishes this verb from the separate noun sense “order, government directive” and gives examples in which an action follows 命, including 命夸娥氏二子负二山.

汉典 analyzes the character as 从口从令 and explains the composition as orally issuing an order; its quoted 《说文》 gloss is 使也, and the quoted commentary explains 令 as 发号. The Academia Sinica database describes the historical graph as adding 口 to emphasize oral issuance. Zhao's article also discusses the early overlap of 命 and 令. These sources support a command-related reading of the components, but do not establish that every modern sense of 命 derives from this verb sense.

The dictionary definitions of 招募 support this overall sense; 招 has senses involving calling people over or publicly bringing them in, while 募 is glossed as broadly seeking or soliciting. The supplied sense is not limited to military recruitment: dictionary examples include 招募贤士 and recruiting technical personnel. The military examples in the Hou Hanshu and Romance of the Three Kingdoms show particular contexts, not a restriction on the word's meaning.

sources.title: 时间词“一会（儿）”的时点指称功
sources.summary_en: This linguistic study distinguishes duration-reference 一会（儿） from a later time-position use. It analyzes 一会（儿） after a verb as measuring the action's duration and argues that the duration expression developed from 一 + 会, initially interpreted as ‘one gathering.’ The study proposes that comparison with separation helped yield a short-time meaning, which lexicalized by the Song period; it then traces a distinct time-position use through grammaticalization. These historical links are the study's analysis, not direct proof that modern duration 一会儿 is synchronically composed as ‘one gathering.’

The study's proposed historical analysis takes 一会 back to the phrase 一 + 会, ‘one gathering,’ and suggests that contrast with separation could make the interval seem short. It reports that the short-duration use became lexicalized by the Song period. This is an argued historical pathway, not evidence that the parts retain those meanings in modern 一会儿.

The study distinguishes duration 一会（儿） from a time-position use that can mean ‘after a short while’ in suitable contexts, and proposes that the latter developed through grammaticalization from duration use in adverbial contexts. Wu Ting’s study analyzes 到处 as developing from phrases meaning ‘the place(s) reached’: 到 contributes reaching or arrival and 处 contributes place. The study describes a later adverbial use equivalent to 处处. This is the study’s proposed historical account, not an independently established derivation.

The study distinguishes early linear adjacency of 到 and 处, which it says was not yet a word, from phrase uses it analyzes as ‘places reached’ and from the later adverbial use. It reports that the adverbial function becomes visible in examples where 到处 modifies a predicate, while some earlier examples remain phrases. Thus an isolated old occurrence spelled 到处 cannot automatically be treated as an attestation of the modern word or as proof of its derivation.

sources.title: The Diachronic Development of Passive Constructions from Archaic Chinese to Modern Mandarin
sources.summary_en: Yin Li’s 2015 dissertation proposes a relationship between transitive 被 meaning ‘suffer’ and the later 被 marker in agentless passives. It discusses a proposed metaphorical extension from covering to suffering as an earlier account by other scholars, distinguishing that proposal from Li’s own proposed connection. The accessible dissertation text identifies Western and Eastern Han discussion, but the material opened here does not establish a precise date when 被 became a productive passive marker.

sources.title: A reevaluation of so-called passive constructions in ancient Chinese: from Pre-Qin to the Han dynasty
sources.summary_en: Jianhong Zeng’s 2020 dissertation argues that the ancient items traditionally called passive markers, including 被, could also occur in non-passive uses, and that passive readings depended on context. It concludes that Archaic Chinese markers had a low degree of grammaticalization and questions whether the evidence supports a consistent syntactic passive marker in that period.

claims.text_en: In both supplied examples, 被 marks the clause as passive: 青州 and 卢植 are presented as undergoing the actions 围住 and 诬陷. The agent is overt after 被 in both cases, as 黄巾军 and 人 respectively. The examples do not show 被 contributing a separate tense or aspect meaning.

The dictionary records covering, suffering or undergoing, and passive marking as separate bèi uses. It also reports the older sleeping-garment sense and a commentary describing an extension from that sense to covering or extending over. These recorded senses do not by themselves prove that the passive marker developed from either the garment or covering sense.

Li proposes that transitive 被 meaning ‘suffer’ is related to the later marker in agentless passives. The dissertation also reports an earlier proposal by other scholars that suffering developed metaphorically from covering. These are distinct historical proposals; the evidence opened here does not prove either a covering-to-suffering-to-passive chain or a direct derivation of the modern marker from the garment sense.

The ancient history is disputed: Zeng argues that 被 and other alleged ancient passive markers had non-passive uses as well, with passive interpretation determined by context, and concludes that Archaic Chinese did not have a consistent syntactic passive marker. This complicates any claim that the modern marker’s status or development is securely established by early examples.

施爱东’s account supports a broad historical shift in use: older canonical examples mostly concern precedents, old systems, former work, or historical events; Ming-Qing vernacular examples use 故事 for matter that is told or heard, including material that may be fictional. The same article says literary narrative use was already present by the late Ming, so the translation activity is not evidence that all narrative uses originated from English Story.

A limited component-level observation is possible: 故 can mean 'former' or 'old' in older usages, and 事 can refer to an affair or event; together these fit some older senses of 故事 such as 'former affairs' or 'precedent.' The 2024 article proposes a broader shared 'affair' basis, but isolated component senses and older compound uses do not prove that the current narrative meaning is compositionally derived from them. sources.summary_en: Records 摇 as the 《說文》 gloss for 掉, and lists a separate sense 落下 with later literary examples. It documents distinct senses of 掉 but does not establish the history of the whole word 掉下.

sources.title: 魏兆惠, 论“掉”及“X掉”的历史演变
sources.summary_en: This historical study argues that 掉 developed a fall sense from earlier movement senses. It describes Han-period vertical-motion uses as a basis for the fall sense, gives Tang evidence for 掉 used alone with a fall meaning, and reports more frequent such uses in Song material. The article also discusses X掉 constructions, which are not evidence for the history of 掉下.

sources.title: 主体+动词+趋向补语 Dp+参照点(+Dd)
sources.summary_en: This linguistic study describes modern Chinese postverbal directional elements as expressing path in motion events, and identifies verb-plus-directional-complement structures. It supports the general constructional analysis but does not specifically discuss 掉下.

sources.title: 关于汉语的“下”和“～下”
sources.summary_en: The record concerns 下 and postverbal ～下, but the page required JavaScript and robot verification, so its research content could not be checked.

claims.text_en: The dictionary defines 掉下 as 往下落, so its supplied sense is supported as falling downward. The entry does not require a particular height, agent, cause, or manner; the horse in the example supplies a higher starting position for that occurrence.

In the target sense, 下 contributes downward direction: the Ministry dictionary separately gives 下 the verbal meaning 'move from high to low; descend.' Together with the compound definition, this supports a compositional reading of 掉下 as falling downward. The exact syntactic label for 下 in this compound is not established by the compound dictionary entry.

掉 has a documented fall sense as well as older movement senses. The character dictionary records the older gloss 摇 and a distinct 落下 sense; therefore the modern fall meaning need not be attributed to 下 alone.

Wei's study argues for a historical development of 掉 from 摇 toward 落: it treats Han uses involving vertical movement as a basis for the later fall sense and cites Tang examples of 掉 used alone with a fall meaning, with more examples in Song texts. This supports a history for 掉's fall sense, but does not prove a particular derivation or date for the exact compound 掉下.

A verb followed by a directional complement is a recognized modern Chinese construction for expressing a motion path. This makes a verb-plus-direction interpretation of 掉下 plausible, but the opened grammar study does not analyze this specific word, so the precise constructional account remains unverified.

parts.contribution_en: As a verb, it means to aid someone in difficulty or danger.

sources.summary_en: The entry glosses 救 as 止 and analyzes it as 攴 plus phonetic 求. Duan Yucai quotes the Analects and Ma Rong’s gloss 救猶止也, then comments on the relation between 救 and 止.

sources.title: 漢語多功能字庫：救
sources.summary_en: The database analyzes the character as 攴 plus phonetic 求. It interprets 攴 as a hand holding a stick and says bronze uses include 解救、救援, citing the Qin Wang Zhong and Zhongshan Wang Fanghu inscriptions. This is the database’s interpretation of the forms and examples.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 救 means to aid and help someone out of difficulty or danger. The dictionary’s definition does not specify a method or type of danger, so the broad gloss “save; rescue” fits. The example gives no further detail about what or whom is being rescued.

The component analysis does not transparently encode the modern aid/rescue meaning: the cited analyses assign 求 a phonetic role, while the Shuowen entry gives 攴 as the other component. Shuowen glosses 救 as 止 (“stop”); the modern dictionary also lists a distinct stop/prevent sense. These facts establish the attested glosses and analyses, but do not by themselves prove that the modern aid/rescue sense developed from “stop.”

The CUHK database identifies bronze examples as uses meaning 解救、救援, which supports early attestation of an aid/rescue use according to that source. The examples do not explain how that sense relates historically to the Shuowen gloss 止.

sources.summary_en: Reports the Shuowen Xinfu gloss 匿也 and its note that 臧 was used in the Han Shu and 艹 was added later. The reference says excavated Qin and Han manuscript instances of 藏 are mostly written 臧, and cites 左傳's 掩賊為藏. It connects 藏 and 葬 through burying. These are character-level historical observations; they do not by themselves establish a complete derivation of the modern word.

sources.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「臧」
sources.summary_en: Discusses proposed histories of 臧 and 藏, including the proposal that 臧 was an earlier graph used for hiding or storing and that adding 艹 yielded 藏. It cites manuscript and received-text examples, but presents parts of the semantic account as interpretations or proposals rather than demonstrating that modern cáng 'conceal' developed from 'store'.

claims.text_en: In the target sense, cáng means to conceal or hide: to put or keep someone or something where it is not seen or discovered. The dictionaries support this sense separately from storage. Neither the entry definition nor the supplied example specifies a motive or method; the example shows people hidden on the two sides of a mountain.
Cáng also has a distinct storage or accumulation sense. That sense should not replace the target concealment sense.

The historical and character references report that 藏 was written with 臧 in some earlier records and that 艹 was added later; the character entry analyzes 臧 as phonetic. This describes the graph’s history, but does not make 艹 an independently supported semantic explanation of the target word.

Older sources attest concealment uses, including the traditional gloss 藏，匿也, and also attest storage uses. A specialist reference proposes a relationship between 臧, 藏, hiding, and storing, but the attested older spellings and senses alone do not establish that the modern concealment sense derived from the storage sense.

claims.text_en: In the target sense, 接着 presents an event or action as following the preceding one; it commonly suggests close succession or continuation. The word marks the sequence and does not itself identify the following action.

In the supplied example, 接着 introduces the event of their drinking 酒 in the garden as following a previously narrated event. The example alone does not specify the kind of alcoholic drink or the interval between events.

The references support a synchronic contrast between 接着’s physical catching sense and its senses of continuing or following. They do not explain what individual 接 and 着 contribute to the temporal use, so a compositional account of the parts is not established by the sources opened.

The 2025 article summarizes a proposed development from verb 接着 through adverbial and connective uses to discourse-marker use, while noting that multiple uses coexist. The opened source does not supply historical stages or attestations proving that this sequence is the derivation of the target temporal use; an older attested sense of ‘follow closely’ alone would not prove that derivation.

sources.title: 涿州 — 太平寰宇记
sources.summary_en: The Song geographical work says the Han 涿郡 was named after 涿水 and locates a 涿水 near the county. This is an explicit historical etymological account, but it is not independent proof of the derivation.

sources.title: 水经注卷十二 — 水经注
sources.summary_en: Li Daoyuan reports earlier statements that 涿郡 lay south of 涿水, then proposes that 涿 was named from the water and that the commandery and county inherited that name. He qualifies this as possibly close but not secure, so the text supports a reported hypothesis rather than a settled derivation.

sources.title: 郡 — Ministry of Education Revised Mandarin Dictionary
sources.summary_en: Defines 郡 as the name of an ancient Chinese local administrative region and describes its changing relation to 县 across periods. This supports the administrative contribution of 郡 in 涿郡.

claims.text_en: 郡 contributes the administrative classification “commandery”: the dictionary defines it as an ancient local administrative region, and CHGIS classifies this 涿郡 as a commandery with 涿县 as its seat. “Zhuo Commandery” is therefore supported as a rendering of the name.
涿 is the inherited proper-name element in 涿郡, also found in the seat name 涿县. The gazetteer and character dictionary document these names but do not by themselves explain the origin of 涿.

Historical sources offer a water-name explanation, with differing levels of certainty. 水经注 proposes that 涿郡 and 涿县 took 涿 from 涿水, but explicitly qualifies the proposal as uncertain. 太平寰宇记 states more directly that the Han commandery was named after 涿水. These attest a historical explanation; they do not independently establish the derivation.

The Shuowen Jiezi tradition glosses 涿 as flowing or dripping downward and analyzes it as 从水，豖声. The sources opened do not connect that lexical gloss to the historical place-name, so it should not be used as an explanation of 涿郡.

sources.summary_en: The article abstract contrasts 一直, which describes continuing states or feelings, with 总, which expresses repeated actions or states. It notes that they can overlap when discussing event frequency in a specified time.

sources.title: 频率副词“不断”的词汇化过程
sources.summary_en: The accessible article page identifies a study about the lexicalization of 不断 and summarizes that topic. It does not show the historical discussion about 一直; the linked full-text PDF could not be fetched.

claims.text_en: In the supplied example, 一直 gives 叹气 a continuing temporal span. The sentence does not specify how long Liu Bei sighs or how many sighs occur; interpreting the activity as one unbroken physical sigh would add detail the sentence does not supply.

For this target use, 一直 marks continuity within a relevant time span. The linguistic article distinguishes this continuing profile from the repeated-event profile associated with 总, while allowing overlap in frequency contexts; therefore 一直 should not be reduced to habitual recurrence across separate occasions.
The dictionary also lists directional 一直 and a sense meaning a stretch of a journey. These recorded uses do not, on their own, demonstrate a historical derivation of the temporal continuity sense.

guides.explanation_en: 兵 means soldiers or troops: people serving in a military force, individually or as a group. It does not specify a branch or rank.

parts.contribution_en: Refers to soldiers or troops as military personnel.

sources.title: 漢字「兵」：基本資料
sources.summary_en: Academia Sinica’s character database lists senses including weapons, soldiers/troops, and military affairs. It supports the supplied sense coverage, but does not explain how the senses developed.

sources.summary_en: Taiwan’s Ministry of Education dictionary lists 兵 for weapons, warriors or armies, military affairs, and the lowest-ranking members of a military force. It gives literary examples for the weapon and warrior/army senses, including cited uses in 戰國策 and 文選.

sources.summary_en: The dictionary’s editorial entry quotes Shuowen Jiezi’s gloss 械 and its description of 兵 as 廾 holding 斤. This supports what that historical dictionary says about the character’s form and gloss; it does not by itself demonstrate the historical development of the soldiers/troops sense.

sources.title: 漢字「兵」：字形演變
sources.summary_en: Academia Sinica’s character-evolution page describes the upper part as 斤, an axe-shaped tool also used as a weapon, and the lower part as two hands holding the tool or weapon. It does not establish a derivation from the weapon sense to the people sense.

claims.text_en: The supplied sense, “soldiers; troops,” is supported directly: Academia Sinica lists 士卒 and 軍隊, and the Ministry of Education dictionary groups 戰士 and 軍隊 under a sense of 兵. These definitions do not specify a branch or other subtype.

The character’s form is described as two hands holding 斤, an axe-shaped tool that could also serve as a weapon. Shuowen Jiezi’s quoted gloss is 械. This supports a weapon-related form and historical gloss, but does not by itself explain the soldiers/troops sense.

The Ministry of Education dictionary records both a weapon sense and a warriors/army sense, with literary examples for each. The opened sources do not establish the specific historical path from one sense to the other, so the proposed weapon-to-soldier derivation remains unverified here.

guides.explanation_en: 草席 is a woven mat made of grass: 草 gives its material, and 席 names the mat.

parts.contribution_en: Specifies grass as the material.
Names a woven mat.

sources.title: 〈席〉— Ministry of Education 《Concised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary》
sources.summary_en: Defines one sense of 席 as a woven pad made from grass stems, bamboo strips, and similar materials for sitting or lying, with 草席 among its examples. The broad material list describes 席 generally; it does not establish that 草席 includes bamboo mats.

sources.title: 席 — 教育百科 | 教育雲線上字典
sources.summary_en: The page reproduces several Taiwan Ministry of Education dictionary entries. The revised dictionary gives an older citation using 草蓆 in a description of someone sleeping on a grass mat; the entries also distinguish the mat sense of 席 from senses such as seat, position, banquet, and classifier.

claims.text_en: In the target sense, 草席 is compositionally transparent: 草 identifies the grass material, while 席 names the woven mat. A dictionary entry for 草席 itself defines it as a mat woven from dried grass; the Ministry of Education entry for 席 describes the broader mat category as woven from grass stems, bamboo strips, and similar materials. That broader range for 席 does not show that 草席 includes bamboo mats.

The example’s 草席 is the physical mat sense, not other senses of 席 such as ‘seat,’ ‘position,’ ‘banquet,’ or a classifier. The Qing compilation quotes 草席 in a Ming gazetteer entry and a poem attributed to Ouyang Zhan, but these citations do not establish the compound’s origin or a specific path of development.

The available direct definition supports ‘grass mat’ but does not specify whether the target word also covers mats made from other plant materials. The example only names the item as 草席 and supplies no further material detail.

guides.explanation_en: 天 means heaven or sky, and 地 means earth or ground. Together, 天地 names heaven and earth as a whole, which may be invoked as witnesses in a traditional oath or wedding rite.
guides.caveat_en: The ritual use comes from the practice of invoking heaven and earth; 天地 itself does not mean “wedding.”

guides.explanation_en: 高兴 means feeling happy or pleased. 高 adds an elevated, positive quality to 兴, which contributes the sense of mood or spirits; together they describe a cheerful state of mind.
guides.caveat_en: The word conventionally means happy or pleased; it does not imply literal height or a particular cause for the feeling.

parts.contribution_en: Adds an elevated, positive quality.

guides.explanation_en: 后来 is a conventional time word meaning “later” or “afterward” in a sequence. 后 points to what is after; together the word locates a subsequent time.

parts.contribution_en: After or subsequent in a sequence.

sources.summary_en: Hilary M. Chappell's 2022 study discusses comparative degree markers across Sinitic varieties. It analyzes dialectal 同样 as combining a morpheme meaning 'same' with one meaning 'kind'; this supports a component-based analysis but does not establish the historical development of the standard-language noun-modifying use.

claims.text_en: In the supplied sentence, 同样的 modifies 想法 and means that the three people have the same or alike ideas. The sentence does not specify that their ideas match in every detail.

A supported synchronic component analysis is that 同 contributes 'same' and 样 contributes 'form' or 'kind', giving a sense like 'of the same kind/form' that fits the target use. The grammar study explicitly analyzes dialectal 同样 this way, while the Ministry dictionary independently lists these component meanings. This evidence does not prove a historical derivation of the modern compound.

The learner study reports that cited grammar references also describe 同样 modifying verbs and linking clauses with a meaning consistent with the preceding clause. Those are adjacent uses, distinct from the noun-modifying phrase in the supplied example.

The dictionary cites 少有大志 in the Ma Yuan biography, and the opened text contains that wording. This supports an older attestation of 大志 used aspirationally; the passage alone does not prove a particular historical derivation of the modern word.

claims.text_en: In the supplied example, 悬念 concerns the unresolved question of whether Dong Zhuo survives: the story leaves his fate open and invites expectation about the outcome. This is the narrative sense of audience anticipation, not the personal sense of being concerned about someone.

As a cautious synchronic reading of the word’s parts, 悬 can evoke a hanging or unresolved state, while 念 contributes the sense of thinking about, keeping in mind, or mental attention. Together these meanings fit expectation focused on an unsettled plot or fate. The opened sources do not establish this as the proven historical derivation of the narrative sense.

悬念 also has a distinct personal-concern sense. The Ministry dictionary records it with a Tang attestation; the narrative sense is separately attested in a 1982 quotation cited by 漢典. These attestations document the senses, but do not establish when the narrative sense arose or how it developed from the personal-concern sense.

The examples document those uses but do not establish how the modern emotional sense developed from them.

sources.title: 开 kāi、jiān、qiān - 汉典
sources.summary_en: The entry records 开 as opening, unfolding, and instructing or inspiring, among other senses. sources.title: 漢字「心」：基本資料
sources.summary_en: Academia Sinica's character database lists 心 meanings including the heart, inner self, thought, temperament, and disposition. This supports an association with the mental or emotional domain, not a complete derivation of the word 开心.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 开心 means that someone feels happy or pleased: 汉典 defines it as 心情舒畅愉快 and lists 快乐、高兴 as a related dictionary sense. Its definition does not specify a cause, intensity, or particular kind of happiness.

心 contributes a mental or inner-person domain that fits the word's emotional meaning: character references include meanings such as inner self, thought, temperament, and disposition. This supports a component-level association, but does not by itself show the historical formation of the modern word.

开 has attested senses of opening and of instructing or inspiring the mind. An interpretation such as the mind becoming open or eased is compatible with those senses, but the consulted references do not demonstrate that as the historical source of 开心 meaning happy or identify the steps by which that sense arose.

The same spelling is also recorded with distinct senses including enlightening the mind, treating someone frankly, flowering, and joking. These dictionary-listed senses should not be substituted for the supplied happy/pleased sense, and their existence does not establish that any one of them developed into it.

guides.explanation_en: 给 marks the person an action is done to or for, presenting them as its recipient or beneficiary. In 给人治病, 治病 is the action and 给人 identifies the people served by it; the marker does not say whether the action succeeds.

parts.contribution_en: Introduces the person who receives or benefits from an action.

sources.title: 汉韩授予动词语法化的比较
sources.summary_en: This specialist study classifies one prepositional use of 给 as introducing a beneficiary or affected party. It illustrates the service-target use with examples such as 给姨太太捶腿 and 给黛玉盖好被窝. It proposes that this use developed from the giving verb when the thing given was understood as the giver’s action. The article also reports differing accounts of the giving verb’s origin and dating.

claims.text_en: In the supplied sentence, 给 introduces 百姓 as the human target of 张角’s 治病 action: roughly, he treated people for the common people / provided treatment to them. The construction presents them as people served by the action; it does not establish that treatment succeeded or specify Zhang Jue’s motive. The study’s comparable service-target examples support this reading. It also treats transfer recipients as broadly within the beneficiary category, so recipient and beneficiary interpretations can overlap.

The study proposes a development from the giving verb: when the thing construed as given is the giver’s action rather than a concrete object, 给 can be reanalyzed as introducing the person served by that action, with a function comparable to 为 or 替. This is the article’s proposed grammaticalization path; the account does not show that a literal transfer meaning remains in every modern use.

This target use is distinct from 给 as a transfer verb and from 给 introducing an affected object or an agent in passive constructions. The article classifies these as different uses, so the recipient/beneficiary reading in the supplied example should not be replaced by the more familiar concrete-transfer meaning.

sources.summary_en: The dictionary reads 涿郡 as zhuó jùn and defines it as a Han-established commandery located in present-day Zhuozhou, Hebei. This directly attests zhuó for 涿 in 涿郡, but not zhuō in 涿县.

sources.title: 涿郡 — 词典网历史地名
sources.summary_en: This historical-place-name reference says the Western Han 涿郡 was based at 涿县 and attributes to 《寰宇记》 the explanation that the commandery was named after 涿水. This is an attributed explanation for the commandery name, not direct proof of how 涿县 was named.

sources.title: 涿州 — 郡县释名
sources.summary_en: This Ming compilation says the Yan settlement was called 涿邑 and that 涿州 was named after 涿水; it also cites older geographical accounts associating 涿县 and the river. It records historical explanations but does not establish that the county name was originally coined from the river.

claims.text_en: In 涿县, 县 marks the administrative unit as a county. CHGIS classifies 涿县 as a county and locates it at present-day Zhuozhou, Hebei; thus “Zhuo County” fits the supplied sense. 涿 is the distinguishing inherited place-name element, but these sources do not give it a lexical meaning within this name.

CHGIS reports 后晓荣's proposal that a pre-Qin Yan place called 涿都 preceded the Qin/Han 涿县. The cited argument treats 豕 in a seal inscription, 豕都司徒, as 涿 and interprets 涿都 as a county-level administrative place. This is a reported scholarly proposal, not proof that the modern name's 涿 derives from 涿都.

The water-based explanations concern related names but do not settle the origin of 涿县: CHGIS quotes Ying Shao saying 涿水 rises in 涿鹿县, while 词典网 attributes to 《寰宇记》 the claim that 涿郡 was named from 涿水. 郡县释名 likewise says 涿州 was named after 涿水. These statements do not demonstrate that 涿县 itself was formed from the hydronym.

The supplied reading Zhuōxiàn is not directly attested by the opened dictionary entry for 涿县. The character dictionary lists zhuō as an alternate reading, whereas the specific entry 涿郡 is read zhuó jùn. The dictionary evidence therefore does not verify the supplied first-tone reading for this county name.

It treats V开 as a change construction with several subtypes and says that, as its components become more closely integrated, 开 remains as a grammatical marker. sources.summary_en: An accessible conference presentation studies V开 in texts across historical periods. It reports differing prior scholarly accounts of the construction’s semantic development and says some earlier researchers date a post-verbal ‘leave/separate’ use of 开 to around the Tang period. claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 离开 means separating from a person, thing, or place. Both the Ministry of Education dictionary and 汉典 give that scope; 汉典’s room example directly illustrates leaving a location. The evidence does not specify a manner of travel or destination.

离 has a separation or departure sense, with cited examples such as 离居 and 离家. This is relevant character-level support for the 离 portion of 离开, but those examples do not prove how the modern compound formed.

开 is also recorded with a ‘separate, part’ sense, alongside its more familiar ‘open’ senses. That makes a separation-related association possible in 离开, but the consulted evidence does not establish that 开 contributes a distinct, independently identifiable meaning in the modern word.

Research on the broader V开 construction treats it as a construction with multiple change-related readings and discusses grammaticalization. A conference presentation also reports earlier scholars’ proposals that a post-verbal ‘leave/separate’ use of 开 appeared around the Tang period. These construction-level accounts provide historical context for 开 but do not establish that the lexical compound 离开 arose from that development.

claims.text_en: In the supplied sense, 因为 is a conjunction that introduces the reason for a stated event or proposition. The dictionaries describe its causal function without specifying a particular kind of reason.
For this modern causal use, the dictionaries define 因为 as a whole conjunction; they do not assign separate causal meanings to 因 and 为.

The 2023 article distinguishes older sequences in which 因 has a connective sense such as ‘therefore/then’ and 为 continues into the following predicate or passive construction. It interprets certain Song-era vernacular examples as causal 因为, while proposing the specific analysis ‘shortened 原因为（是）’. That proposal is the author's argument; the examples alone do not establish that derivation.

The accessible abstract of Wang's study confirms that it treats 因为 as a connective in a grammaticalization study, but it does not provide a specific historical derivation that would resolve the internal composition of modern 因为.

The supplied English gloss “forge” is narrower than the general physical-object definition. The example involving weapons makes metalworking a plausible contextual interpretation, but the sentence does not state the material or technique; “make” or “manufacture” preserves what is explicit.

The Ministry of Education’s concise dictionary also distinguishes 生存 from 使生存, supporting the distinction between living and causing someone or something to live.

Duan Yucai’s commentary reports an older gloss related to flowing water and explicitly calls the use meaning ‘not dead’ an extension, citing the Odes and Mencius. This documents Duan’s proposed explanation; the page does not provide a dated chain establishing how that extension developed into the ordinary modern verb sense.

sources.title: 浅析“拿”在近代汉语中的用法
sources.summary_en: The article abstract says 拿 appeared later than its variant 拏 and became more widespread in 近代汉语. It surveys 拿 as a verb, preposition, and word-forming morpheme, and studies development from verb to preposition and morpheme. The abstract does not establish a derivation of the target hand-taking sense from 拏’s older gloss.

sources.title: “拿”字语法化的考察
sources.summary_en: The article abstract studies grammatical functions of 拿, particularly disposal, causative, and passive uses, and proposes developments from object to disposal to causative and from object to passive. Those are grammaticalized uses, not evidence for how the supplied concrete taking or holding sense originated.

sources.title: 拏 ná、ráo - 汉典
sources.summary_en: Collects several senses and textual glosses for 拏, including holding or taking and pulling or drawing along. Its reproduced 說文注 describes textual confusion between 持 and 牽引 glosses. These entries attest older glosses but do not prove a direct derivation of modern 拿’s target sense.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 拿 means taking something by hand or holding it. The dictionaries do not specify a particular grip or require that the object be carried away. The same spelling also has separately listed senses such as catching, using, and controlling or managing.

The character reference describes 拿 as a form used in place of 拏 and says it later became an independent standard character. It reports an older 說文 gloss of 拏 as 牽引, ‘pull or draw along,’ but this character history alone does not establish that the modern hand-taking or holding sense developed from that gloss.

The 說文 textual record is reported as variable: the reference for 挐 associates 持 (‘hold’) and 牽引 (‘pull or draw along’) with differently written forms in 大徐本 and 段注本. These records do not resolve the semantic pathway to the modern 拿 sense.

A study of 拿 in 近代汉语 reports that 拏 is an older variant and that 拿 itself appeared later and became more common. Its abstract traces verbal uses toward prepositional and morpheme uses, but does not demonstrate the origin of the concrete hand-taking or holding sense.

A separate grammaticalization study concerns 拿’s disposal, causative, and passive functions. Its proposed pathways address those grammatical functions and should not be treated as an explanation for the supplied concrete sense.

claims.text_en: For the supplied physical-action sense, 刺 contributes piercing or thrusting with something sharp. This is the relevant dictionary sense; the separate assassination and figurative-criticism senses do not explain this use.
Read zhòng, 中 contributes the result of hitting or landing on the target, consistent with the dictionary’s ‘fit/be directly on target’ sense and the direct 刺中 definition.
Together, 刺中 means to pierce or thrust and hit the target. The word-level sources do not specify a weapon, target identity, or injury severity; those details must come from context.

guides.explanation_en: 百姓 is the conventional word for ordinary people in general, also called “the people” or “citizens.” Its modern meaning is not simply “one hundred surnames.”
guides.caveat_en: The characters 百 (“hundred”) and 姓 (“surname”) do not give a reliable word-by-word explanation of the modern meaning.

sources.title: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》：百姓
sources.summary_en: The dictionary gives two senses: an older 百官族姓 sense, with an explanation connecting it to nobles' surnames, and a broad sense meaning ordinary people or citizens. Its examples for the latter include a citation from the Book of Changes.

sources.title: “百姓”原指奴隶主
sources.summary_en: A People's Daily Overseas Edition article hosted by Xinhua asserts that 百姓 referred to nobles or officials before becoming a commoner term. It also proposes a specific origin involving an alliance of about one hundred clans and captives; the article's opened text does not provide independent corroboration for that account.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 百姓 means people generally, ordinary people, or citizens. The Ministry of Education dictionary records this as a broad sense, distinct from its older 百官族姓 sense; the supplied example glosses fit the broad sense.

The dictionary's older gloss 百官族姓 connects the expression with officials and clans or surnames, but this does not by itself explain how the current broad sense developed. The opened sources do not establish a word-by-word derivation of modern 百姓 from the contributions of 百 and 姓.

The Xinhua article asserts a particular prehistoric account involving roughly one hundred clans and captives. That account is not established by the Ministry of Education dictionary, and the opened Fudan page is a book announcement rather than evidence for that account or the proposed semantic pathway. Treat the specific origin story as unsupported by this source set.

guides.explanation_en: Before an action phrase, 要 marks the subject’s desire or intention to do that action. Whether it sounds more like wanting or intending depends on context; 要 alone does not specify how firmly settled the intention is.

parts.contribution_en: Marks the subject’s desire or intention to perform the following action.

sources.title: 现代汉语词典（第七版）
sources.summary_en: The yào entry labels the target construction as an auxiliary expressing the will to do something and gives 他要学游泳. It lists this separately from wanting to obtain or keep something, needing or having to do something, and imminent-future 要.

sources.title: 要 yāo、yào - 汉典
sources.summary_en: The entry separately lists yào ‘wish/want to’ and yào ‘be going to,’ among other senses. Its Shuowen section reports the graph’s older association with the waist/body; that graph history alone does not establish the origin of the modern volitional use.

sources.title: The semantic historical development of modal verbs of volition in Chinese
sources.summary_en: In this chapter, Alain Peyraube and Li Ming describe modern 要 as expressing intention/want and propose a historical path from request/ask to want, with older examples. They also caution that the history of modal auxiliaries is complex and early uses are not always clear. This is a scholarly proposed development, not by itself proof that every current volitional use derives by that path.

sources.title: “Wanting” the future: The case of future yao
sources.summary_en: Huang, van Dooren, and Mendes distinguish modern desire, deontic/teleological, and future uses. They report that desire 要 is attested later than the request/demand and deontic uses, by the Tang period, while the origin of non-desire future 要 is debated: it may derive from desire 要 or deontic/teleological 要.

sources.title: The semantic historical development of modal verbs of volition in Chinese
sources.summary_en: The publisher page identifies the chapter’s authors as Alain Peyraube and Li Ming and places it in Newest Trends in the Study of Grammaticalization and Lexicalization in Chinese (2012), pp. 149–168. The chapter content is restricted on this page; historical claims here are supported by the opened chapter text at s3.

claims.text_en: In the target use, 要 precedes an action phrase and marks the subject’s will or intention to do that action. The dictionary gives an auxiliary example and distinguishes this use from wanting an object and from imminent-future 要.

The supplied examples fit the shared volitional contribution: the characters want or intend to enlist or kill someone. Their contexts do not require a finer distinction between a wish and a settled intention, or establish a particular degree of commitment.

The word has no linked subcomponents in the supplied entry. Although the source reports a historical graph association with the waist/body, this does not explain the present volitional meaning; no meaningful written part can be assigned a separate contribution to that meaning from the opened evidence.

Peyraube and Li propose a historical development from request/ask uses of 要 toward ‘want’; their chapter gives examples for these uses. This is evidence for a scholarly derivational account, but the older senses and examples do not alone prove the full derivation of the present-day volitional auxiliary.

Historical work distinguishes the desire use from the deontic/teleological and future uses. For future 要, one study reports disagreement over whether it developed from desire or from deontic/teleological 要; that debate does not settle every detail of the history of the modern desire/intention use.

guides.explanation_en: 当时 refers to a contextually identified time: “at that time” or “then.” 当 contributes the sense of being at or during a time, and 时 names the time; together they point to the time in question.

parts.contribution_en: Contributes the sense of being at or during a time.
Names the time being referred to.

sources.title: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》：當時
sources.summary_en: The dictionary defines dāngshí as ‘formerly; at that time’ and illustrates it with a quotation from the Xunzi. It also lists ‘immediately; at once’ under the same pronunciation.

sources.title: 漢語網：當時詞語解釋／當時是什麽意思
sources.summary_en: This dictionary describes dāngshí as the time previously mentioned or referred to, and as the time when a past event occurred. It assigns ‘at that moment; immediately’ to dàngshí and lists additional historical uses, including ‘people of the time,’ ‘the reigning emperor,’ ‘in one’s prime,’ and ‘timely.’ Its pronunciation assignment for ‘immediately’ differs from the MOE dictionary.

sources.title: “当”的演变过程
sources.summary_en: The article discusses 当 before temporal expressions in examples such as 当今 and 当是时, analyzing it there as ‘at/during’ and as a preposition developed from a verb use. It does not establish that the modern word 当时 derives from that construction.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 当时 refers to a contextually identified time, commonly rendered ‘at that time’ or ‘then.’ The example uses it for the period when the epidemic was widespread. The dictionaries support this broad temporal reading; ‘then’ is a contextual paraphrase rather than evidence for a separate component meaning.

时 supplies the time reference in the compound. The role of 当 in the modern word is less certain: the temporal use of 当 before a time expression is attested in constructions such as 当是时, but that parallel does not demonstrate the historical formation or precise contribution of 当时 as a lexical item.

The dictionaries also record an ‘immediately; at once’ use, but disagree about its pronunciation: the MOE dictionary places it under dāngshí, while 漢語網 assigns it to dàngshí. 漢語網 additionally lists historical uses such as ‘people of the time,’ ‘the reigning emperor,’ ‘in one’s prime,’ and ‘timely’; these are distinct from the supplied ordinary temporal sense.
